name: Fractal Depth-Typing & Relationship Granularity (the DEPTH axis of the graph substrate)
description: Andrew-direct 2026-06-30 (make LD-0229 a PRD): establish fractal depth-typing + relationship granularity as a FOUNDATIONAL layer of the graph substrate. Every investigation needs TWO coordinates: BREADTH (where on the surface -- COMPUNIFY surfaces) + DEPTH (how deep / what grain -- estate->layer->resource->script->function->statement; bucket->key->object). Today the substrate is breadth-aware but DEPTH-FLAT -- nodes carry a surface/layer but no declared grain coordinate, so tooling cannot scope its investigation by depth (a 'what writes this S3 key' query can't tell resource-grain from function-grain; the infra island [resource grain] and the compute island [function grain] are disconnected, EC2-RUNS->PipelineScript missing). THE PRINCIPLE (MSTR Tier-0, LD-0229): the node/edge TYPE SYSTEM + INVARIANTS are scale-INVARIANT; granularity = a DECLARED `level` coordinate on a stable CONTAINS ladder, NEVER a type fork; same edge semantics/invariants/tools at every zoom -> ONE graph + ONE toolset + ONE gate-set serve every granularity without per-level re-engineering (scale-free cognition). 4 invariants (declared-level / edges-once-by-semantic-stable-across-grain / existential-rollup-consistency / one-home-at-every-scale) + 3 CTO boundary conditions (semantic-shift: type-set grows by semantic not depth; bounded-materialization: size-invariant in logic, lazy/bounded in materialization; type-specific-drilldown-depth). Grounded keystones verified @ head (Pipeline-CONTAINS-Script-CONTAINS-Function; S3_BUCKET-OWNED_BY-S3Key; EC2-RUNS-PipelineScript cross-stratum seam; TSGRAPH precedent). GOVERNANCE: GRAPHUNI(~D) POPULATES the depth ladders; COMPUNIFY(~C) GOVERNS the grain schema (comp-coverage-map grain_contract + comp-coverage-check rules 7-9, stable_grain landed 01af67fcc); tools READ+CALIBRATE by grain (COMPUNIFY S4 tool-grain calibration). The DEPTH axis composes with the BREADTH axis (GRAPHUNI/COMPUNIFY) + one-home.
